theorem_title: Lemma 2.4 — exact limiting rate and half-erasure ambiguity
formal_statement:
namespace ExpandingCodes.PolynomialStretch

open Filter
/-- Lemma 2.4: the exact continuous-uniform limiting rate and the half-erasure limit. -/
theorem auxiliary_rate (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 / 2)
    (g : ∀ n, Geometry (dimension ε) n) :
    1 / 2 - ε / 8 ≤ limitingRate (dimension ε) ∧
    limitingRate (dimension ε) < 1 / 2 ∧
    Tendsto (fun n => (Module.finrank (g n).F (auxiliaryCode (g n)) : ℝ) /
      rowCount (dimension ε) n) atTop (nhds (limitingRate (dimension ε))) ∧
    Tendsto (fun n => erasureExpectation (auxiliaryCode (g n)) (1 / 2) /
      rowCount (dimension ε) n) atTop (nhds 0) := by sorry

end ExpandingCodes.PolynomialStretch
natural_language_statement:
Fix $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ and the parameter $d=2\lceil512\varepsilon^{-2}\rceil$. For the auxiliary code $B$ in equation (5), put $r=\dim_{F_q}B$ and $m=q^d$. Along the construction as $n\to\infty$,
$$\frac r m\longrightarrow\rho_d=\Pr\!\left[\sum_{j=1}^dX_j\le(d-3)/2\right],\qquad \frac12-\frac\varepsilon8\le\rho_d<\frac12,$$
where the $X_j$ are independent uniform variables on $[0,1]$. If each coordinate is erased independently with probability $1/2$, then
$$\frac{\mathbb E\dim_{F_q}B_E}{m}\longrightarrow0.$$
These assertions hold for every compatible family of finite fields and public row orders. The rate is computed from the actual evaluation subspace, not fixed by definition to one half.

This result supplies both the exact rate bound and the erasure-dimension estimate needed by the distinguisher.

Differences from the source:
- encoding: independent continuous uniforms and asymptotic ratios for the code B → Lebesgue volume of a measurable subset of the unit cube and limits along the construction n→∞; reason: the unit cube has product-uniform probability one, and the construction field sizes tend to infinity
- encoding: r=dim B and E dim B_E → Mathlib finrank of the generalized evaluation span and a finite Bernoulli-weighted sum; reason: these compute the same dimensions and expectation without an integrability premise
